sections.h2: How do Rome owners usually sell a house in a hurry?
sections.html:
A Rome owner can hire a realtor, go it alone, or let a cash buyer take the house as it is. Each has a place. The best fit depends on the house's age, its repair list, and whether a tenant or a co-heir also has a say.

Rome has a large rental share, and that shapes how houses change hands. Owners live in 49.2% of homes, so about half of the housing is rented. Landlords, heirs of a family house and owners of an older home often do better with a plain cash sale than with a long listing.

  • Cash buyer: one walk-through, an offer soon after, no repair work and a closing day that suits you.
  • Realtor sale: the best shot at full market value for a house in good order, at the cost of showings, an inspection and a lender's calendar.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you carry the pricing, the contract and every buyer question.

Total what each route would leave you after fees, repairs, and the months of taxes, insurance and utilities you cover while waiting.

Rome is the Floyd County seat in northwest Georgia, where the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers meet. Its population is 38,934 as of mid-2025, against 37,713 at the 2020 count and 36,303 in 2010. Growth since the April 2020 estimates base is 2.7%, so the market is steady rather than fast-moving.

  • Ownership and value: owners occupy 49.2% of homes, and the middle owner's home is worth $234,300 (2020-2024).
  • Monthly costs: owners with a mortgage pay a middle figure of $1,526, and renters pay $1,032.
  • Households and size: 14,983 households spread over 31.68 square miles of land.

Those are citywide figures. A written offer or an appraisal on your own address tells you far more than a citywide middle value, especially for an older house or one with tenants.

sections.h2: Zoning, variances and the Board of Adjustments
sections.html:
Rome and Floyd County share a Unified Land Development Code, and the city posts it with a 2040 Comprehensive Plan on its Board of Adjustments page. Planning staff take appointments for questions about a property, a project or a request.

Requests that go to the Board of Adjustments include appeals of an administrator's decision, special exceptions, hardship variances and flood protection variances. It meets on the third Thursday at 2:30 in the upstairs Commission Chambers at City Hall, 601 Broad Street. An application must arrive by 5:00 p.m. on the 25th, and the earliest hearing is two months after that date.

  • Special exceptions: relief from setbacks, building height, lot width, street frontage, buffers, signs and parking requirements.
  • Hardship variances: granted only for extraordinary property conditions such as size, shape or topography, or for unnecessary hardship. They are never granted for a condition the applicant created, a use the zoning does not allow, or added dwelling units.
  • Waiting period: after a denial, a request for the same property cannot return for 12 months unless the board shortens the wait.

If your house has a nonconforming addition, a garage apartment or a setback problem, raise it with planning staff before a buyer's survey does. A cash buyer can live with the problem, and a lender may not.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Floyd County assessment
sections.html:
Send a letter to the Floyd County Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. Allowed grounds are taxability, uniformity, value, or a denied homestead exemption.

Assessors and appraisal staff review the file and may raise, lower or keep the figure. If it stays, the appeal goes straight on to the Board of Equalization. If it changes, you have 21 days to contest the new figure in writing. The county offers four formal routes.

Appeal routeGrounds allowedDeadline or time limit
Board of EqualizationAny groundsWritten appeal inside 45 days; its decision can go to Superior Court within 30 days
Hearing OfficerValue or uniformity only; non-homesteaded parcel valued over $1 millionCounty has 90 days to review
Binding arbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer has 45 days after the county's acknowledgment to submit a certified appraisal
Superior CourtAny groundsAppeal within 45 days of the notice; fees apply

sections.h2: What is recorded when a Rome sale closes?
sections.html:
Before a Rome deed can be recorded, the state transfer tax has to be paid. The clerks' cooperative that runs the PT-61 portal treats it as an excise tax on real property sales, and the filer prints one PT-61 to go with the deed.

In Rome, recording happens at the Floyd County clerk's office. Ask your settlement agent who owes the tax under your contract and which rate fits your deed. Ask also for a draft closing statement ahead of time, so you can check the payoff, any tax balance and the split of costs before you sign.

If the house is part of an estate, the person with legal authority to sell has to sign, and the closing office will ask for the papers that prove it. Sort that out first, since a buyer cannot close without it.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Rome house?
sections.html:
Cash is worth pricing out in these Rome situations:

  • A landlord selling a rental with tenants in place, or one left in rough shape by a departing tenant.
  • A family house near downtown that needs a roof, wiring or foundation work.
  • An estate in which heirs live in different states and cannot manage repairs.
  • A seller with a mortgage in arrears who needs a closing date before the lender's deadline.

Ask for a written offer, an explanation of who pays closing costs and a closing date. Then compare it with a listing's likely net. A cash buyer takes on the repairs, so the lower price should be weighed against what fixing the house yourself would cost in money and months.

sections.h2: Getting ready to sell in Rome
sections.html:
1. Find out whether your house has any nonconforming feature, such as an addition, a garage apartment or a setback issue, by asking planning staff.
  2. If you disagree with your value, count 45 days from the date on the notice and mail your letter to the Board of Assessors.
  3. If tenants live in the house, gather the lease and any deposit record.
  4. Compare a written cash offer with a realtor's opinion of value and your carrying costs.
  5. Choose the settlement agent who will file the PT-61 and record the deed.

faqs.q: Is Rome, Georgia, a renter-heavy market?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners occupy 49.2% of homes in the 2020-2024 figures, so about half the housing is rented. That shapes who buys and who sells.

faqs.q: What is the window for contesting a Floyd County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the date the notice was mailed, by letter to the Board of Assessors. A changed value opens a further 21 days to contest the new figure.

faqs.q: Who handles variance requests in Rome?
faqs.a: The joint Rome and Floyd County Board of Adjustments. It sits on third Thursdays at City Hall and wants applications by the 25th of the month. Planning staff will book a time to talk through your request.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rome house that has code or permit problems?
faqs.a: Yes, though you should disclose them. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, and a lender may insist on a fix first. Ask planning staff what the city's file shows for the address.

faqs.q: Which papers record a Rome deed?
faqs.a: Floyd County's clerk receives the deed together with a PT-61 form, after the transfer tax is paid. You complete the form online, and the settlement agent typically files it.
